description: Severity table from INITIAL_INSTRUCTIONS.md as data. Facts come from rules/Facts.kt. Wording is plain language and hedged: 'looks', 'can', never 'is malicious'. Each rule names the check (report section) it belongs to. priority orders findings of equal severity (lower first); the top finding supplies the single next step. summary is the short form used in the three lists.

rules.summary: on a published spyware list
rules.reason: {package} matches a published indicator of stalkerware or spyware (listed by: {iocSources}). Some lists also include dual use tools such as remote access or family monitoring apps; the list name tells you which.
rules.remediation: Do not uninstall yet. Preserve the phone as evidence and contact a digital security professional or a domestic violence support service.

rules.summary: on a published spyware list, but visible and from a store
rules.reason: {package} matches a published indicator (listed by: {iocSources}) but is installed from a store, has an icon, and is not disguised. Stalkerware hides; this looks like a monitoring or family app installed openly. Such apps still see what they say they see.
rules.remediation: If you installed {package} yourself, keep it or remove it as you prefer. If you did not, treat this as high: preserve the phone and contact a digital security professional.

rules.summary: contacted a published spyware domain
rules.reason: {package} contacted a domain published as spyware infrastructure.
rules.remediation: Preserve the phone as evidence and contact a digital security professional.

rules.summary: contacted a domain on a published list, but the app is visible and from a store
rules.reason: {package} contacted a domain that appears on a published spyware list, but the app itself is installed from a store, has an icon, and is not disguised. Monitoring and family apps that appear on such lists contact their own servers; that is what this looks like.
rules.remediation: If you installed {package} yourself, keep it or remove it as you prefer. If you did not, treat this as high: preserve the phone and contact a digital security professional.

rules.summary: hidden, not from a store, holds deep access
rules.reason: {package} has no icon, did not come from an app store, and holds accessibility, device admin, or a microphone, camera or location grant. This is the shape of stalkerware.
rules.remediation: Do not uninstall yet. Preserve the phone as evidence and contact a digital security professional.

rules.summary: hidden store app with admin or accessibility
rules.reason: {package} has no icon and holds accessibility or device admin control. It came from an app store, which makes stalkerware less likely but not impossible.
rules.remediation: Open Settings > Apps, find {package}, and decide whether you installed it on purpose. Remove its accessibility or admin access if not.

rules.summary: accessibility service, not an accessibility app
rules.reason: {package} is an enabled accessibility service and is not an accessibility app. Accessibility services can read everything on screen and type on your behalf.
rules.remediation: If you do not use {package} for accessibility, turn it off in Settings > Accessibility. If you do not recognise it, contact a professional first.

rules.summary: control grant on a package missing from the inventory
rules.reason: {package} holds a control grant (admin, accessibility or notification access) but is not in the app inventory. The inventory may be incomplete on this phone, or the package is hiding.
rules.remediation: Show this report to a professional. Do not change anything yet.

rules.summary: device admin without a work profile
rules.reason: {package} is a device administrator and is not managing a work profile. Device admins can lock or wipe the phone and resist uninstall.
rules.remediation: If you did not set up {package} as an anti theft or work tool, remove its admin rights in Settings > Security > Device admin apps, then uninstall it.

rules.summary: manages a work profile
rules.reason: {package} manages a work profile on this phone. Your employer can see and control the work side, not the personal side.
rules.remediation: Nothing to do if this is your employer's management app.

rules.summary: named like a system component, not one
rules.reason: {package} is named like a system component but is not one and did not come from an app store.
rules.remediation: Uninstall {package} from Settings > Apps unless you know exactly what it is.

rules.summary: installed outside a store, holds a sensitive grant
rules.reason: {package} was installed outside an app store and holds a microphone, camera or location grant.
rules.remediation: If you did not install {package} yourself, uninstall it. If you did, revoke the permissions it does not need.

rules.summary: installed outside a store, no sensitive grants
rules.reason: {package} was installed outside an app store but holds no microphone, camera or location grant.
rules.remediation: Nothing to do if you installed it on purpose.

rules.summary: odd mic, camera or location grant, not from a store
rules.reason: {package} did not come from an app store and holds a microphone, camera or location grant that looks odd for this kind of app.
rules.remediation: Revoke the permission in Settings > Apps > {package} > Permissions, or uninstall it.

rules.summary: odd microphone or background location grant
rules.reason: {package} holds a microphone or background location grant that looks odd for this kind of app. It came from an app store. Foreground location and camera are not counted here; most store apps use them.
rules.remediation: Check Settings > Apps > {package} > Permissions and revoke anything it does not need.

rules.summary: starts at boot and ran over 6 h this week
rules.reason: {package} starts itself at boot and ran in the background for more than 6 hours this week, and it is not a music, messaging, navigation or accessibility app.
rules.remediation: Open Settings > Apps > {package} > Battery and check whether the activity makes sense. Uninstall if you do not use it.

rules.summary: ran over 6 h in the background this week
rules.reason: {package} ran in the background for more than 6 hours this week.
rules.remediation: Nothing to do if you use it a lot.

rules.summary: reads all notifications, not from a store
rules.reason: {package} can read every notification, including messages, did not come from an app store, and is not a messaging or accessibility app.
rules.remediation: Turn off its notification access in Settings > Notifications > Device and app notifications, then uninstall it if you do not recognise it.

rules.summary: reads all notifications (store app)
rules.reason: {package} can read every notification. It came from an app store and is not a messaging app; watch and car companions commonly need this.
rules.remediation: Nothing to do if you set it up. Otherwise turn off its notification access.

rules.summary: listed twice in the inventory
rules.reason: {package} appears twice in the inventory, usually a leftover from a second user or a failed update.
rules.remediation: Nothing to do. Mention it if you talk to a professional.

rules.summary: reports to an unrecognized host on a fixed schedule
rules.reason: {package} looked up {beaconHost} every {beaconInterval} s for the whole monitor window. A fixed schedule to a host that is not a recognized service is how monitoring software reports in. It can also be an ordinary app polling its own server.
rules.remediation: If you do not know what {package} is or why it would report on a schedule, uninstall it. If you do, nothing to do.

rules.summary: sent data with no name lookup
rules.reason: {package} sent about {bytesSentMb} MB during the monitor window without looking up a single name, which means it talks to fixed addresses. Some media and gaming apps do this; so does software that avoids leaving a trail.
rules.remediation: Check Settings > Apps > {package} > Mobile data and Wi Fi usage. If the app has no reason to send that much, uninstall it.

rules.summary: talks to unrecognized hosts and has another oddity
rules.reason: {package} talks to hosts that are not recognized services ({unrecognizedList}) and also has another oddity in this report (install source, a control grant, an odd permission, or heavy background use).
rules.remediation: Review the other finding for {package} first; together they are worth acting on.

rules.summary: talks to unrecognized hosts
rules.reason: {package} talks to hosts that are not on the list of recognized services ({unrecognizedList}). Unrecognized means not on the list; it is not a judgment. Most apps have servers of their own.
rules.remediation: Nothing to do unless the names surprise you.
